senses.gloss: (sec. r. of b. h. to tread, stamp, pile up.
units: Ukts. I, 5 stalks of eatable plants (straw &c.) שבְּסָסָן בגרן which the owner packed in the barn; Succ. 14ᵃ מאי בססן what does this b’sasan mean? R. … says ב׳ ממש he really stamped them (threshed); R. … says התיר אגדן he untied them (for the purpose of piling the stalks closer by treading upon them). [Pesik. Haḥod. p. 45ᵃ; Pesik. R. s. 15 היו בוססות, read with Num. R. s. 11 כּוֹסְסוֹת, v. כָּסַס.]

senses.gloss: (denom. of בָּסִיס) to establish firmly, to found, to put on a secure basis.
units: Cant. R. to I, 9 ומי ב׳ העולם and who gave the world a firm basis?; (ibid. VII, 1; Ruth. R. beg.; Pesik. R. s. 21 ביסם, בישם corr. acc.).—Part. pass. מְבוּסָּס firmly established.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 15">Num. R. s. 15</cite>; Tanḥ. B’haal. 11 <he>כסאו מב׳ למעלן</he> (not <he>מבוסם</he>) His throne is firmly established above, when Israel &c.

senses.gloss: to be firmly established, to rest safely.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> after the Sanctuary was erected <he>נתב׳ העולם</he> the world became firm.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Ib.</cite> as soon as they made a third leg for the table (v. <he>טרסקל</he>), <he>נתב׳</he> it stood firm; Tanḥ. T’rum. 9.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 66">Gen. R. s. 66</cite> <he>נתבשם העולם</he> (corr. acc.); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 811">Yalk. Ps. 811</cite>.
